plan.title: Blood RNA-seq case/control classifier with nested CV
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question is a prediction question, not a differential-expression question: can expression of the 12,000 genes in the 120-sample whole-blood cohort (counts.csv, 12000 x 121 with the gene-ID column; metadata.csv, 120 x 2 with the condition column) separate the 60 cases from the 60 controls, and what accuracy should be expected on a sample the model has never seen. The plan therefore centres on an honest generalisation estimate rather than on a gene list.

T1S1 establishes sample structure first: a design-blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap and library-size summary. This is diagnostic and it is also decisive for interpretation — if cases and controls already separate on PC1 the classifier is easy and the risk is that a technical axis (depth, an unrecorded batch) is doing the work; if they do not separate at all, a high cross-validated AUC later would be the surprising claim and would need scrutiny. The profile records a single batch and no quality flags, so no batch term enters any model; the counts came from Salmon with the length correction not stated, which is noted as an import caveat but does not change the classifier path (the same monotone per-gene transform is applied to every sample).

T1S2 fixes the gene universe with edgeR filterByExpr against the condition factor. This is a cohort-level, condition-blind step that only removes genes with no worthwhile counts anywhere; it defines the candidate feature space and the object the modelling step reads. It is explicitly NOT feature selection — no per-gene ranking, no supervised filter, is allowed to touch the full cohort.

T3S1 is the answer to the question: penalized logistic regression (glmnet, elastic net) with nested cross-validation — lambda and alpha chosen in an inner loop, performance measured only on outer folds whose training never saw the held-out samples. Every supervised operation (normalisation reference, scaling, variance/supervised filtering, feature selection) is refitted inside each training fold, because a selection performed once on all 120 samples is the classic route to an optimistic error estimate. The headline number is the outer-fold ROC AUC with a confidence interval, reported alongside sensitivity, specificity, accuracy at a stated threshold, a calibration check and a label-permutation null. With 60 per class the interval will be wide and the selected gene set will be unstable across folds; both are to be reported, not smoothed over.

T3S2 is deliberately separated from T3S1: only after the unbiased estimate is fixed does a final model get refit on all 120 samples to name the genes carrying signal, with fold-selection frequency reported so that the instability of the panel is visible. Its performance is not re-estimated — the T3S1 number stands as the answer to 'how accurate on a new sample'. T1S3 collects everything into a report with the reproducibility record (seed, session info, package versions), and states plainly the limits: single cohort, no external validation set, so the outer-CV AUC is an internal estimate whose transportability to a new cohort is untested.

steps.method: blind VST + PCA on top 500 variable genes + sample distance heatmap
TMM scaling factors then log-CPM for the classifier feature matrix
Penalized logistic classifier with glmnet, nested cross-validation, and a pROC curve
